clue.text: Most of group left in care, causing local irritation

indicators.note: in places the trimmed group and the L inside the word care

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of signals dropping the final letter of the word for group

parts.note: a bunch is a group
H is the last letter of the word for group, which 'Most of' takes away

explanation.surface: A child taken into care, missing their friends, plays up and upsets the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is only a link; 'local' looks like neighbourhood but means confined to one spot on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A boil-like inflamed swelling on the skin is a very localised irritation.

clue.text: Terrific comic, not second best

indicators.note: not means the letter for second is left out

parts.note: a very funny person is a scream

explanation.surface: A hilarious comedian who still isn't runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The top part of milk rising to the surface stands for the finest of anything.

clue.text: Medic thrust end of stretcher into lift

indicators.note: into puts the main point and the letter inside the lifting word

parts.note: to rear is to lift up
the thrust of an argument is its gist

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of stretcher

explanation.surface: A doctor shoves the end of a stretcher into an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital doctor in training below consultant grade is a kind of medic.

clue.text: Subject to schoolwork, he may get the chance to go on

definitions.text: he may get the chance to go on

parts.note: under means subject to, as in under orders
study is schoolwork

explanation.surface: A pupil kept in for homework hopes to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' is theatrical: to go on stage, replacing an absent actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who learns a role to cover for the lead may be called on stage.

clue.text: Air coming up through middle buttonhole, perhaps

indicators.note: through means passing within, so the gas lies inside the middle

parts.note: the core is the middle

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: air is a gas

explanation.surface: A breeze rising through the centre of a lapel opening.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'coming up' reverses the gas to SAG; 'perhaps' warns that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spray of flowers pinned on is an example of a buttonhole, as the 'perhaps' indicates.

clue.text: Informally christen unbeliever heading off round Thailand

indicators.note: round means the shortened word surrounds the letter
heading off means the first letter goes

parts.note: a gentile is a non-Jew, loosely an unbeliever
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A missionary casually baptises a heathen visiting Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' makes ENTILE from GENTILE; it goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a name or title to something is to christen it in a loose, non-religious sense.

clue.text: Get to eat out with head of firm

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the word firm

parts.note: acid etches metal by eating it out

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to go out for a meal with the company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To go and bring something back is to get it; synonyms in the sense of collect.

clue.text: KO said to cause fracture

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to knock out a boxer is to floor them

explanation.surface: A knockout punch reportedly breaks a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack or break in a material is a defect of that kind.

clue.text: Ringer gets end of bell-rope in a tangle

definitions.note: a tangle here is a coil or twist, a noun

parts.note: a dead ringer is an exact double, a twin

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of bell-rope

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer gets the bottom of the rope knotted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer' suggests a campanologist, as the surface does; it is a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: The twisted strands of string, or a coil and twist of anything, form a tangle.

clue.text: Like the Yeti greeting someone from further east?

parts.note: hi is a greeting
a Malayan comes from the Malay peninsula, further east than the Yeti's home

explanation.surface: The abominable snowman says hello to a visitor from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeti is said to roam the snowy mountain range of Nepal and Tibet, so it belongs to that range.

clue.text: Advanced Guardian leader penned by a couple of journalists

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in an enclosure

parts.note: ED is the crossword abbreviation for editor, a journalist; two of them give the pair

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of Guardian

explanation.surface: The Guardian's editorial was written by two of its reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance slowly and carefully is to inch or sidle forward, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Union engaged in similar outlandish adherence to form

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so the union sits inside the rearranged letters
outlandish means bizarre, so the letters of similar are scrambled

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A union taking part in some similarly strange devotion to procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlandish' rearranges the letters to RIALISM, and 'engaged in' places the union abbreviation within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict insistence on prescribed ceremony and observance is excessive attention to formal procedure.

clue.text: Is rent scam their undoing?

indicators.note: undoing suggests the phrase is unpicked and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a rental fraud brings about the downfall of wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: villains might well be undone by a rent scam, and the phrase undone gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoers and villains, such as fraudsters running a rent scam, are the people meant.

clue.text: No pressure to maintain large part of boat

indicators.note: no means the pressure letter is absent

parts.note: to keep something is to maintain it
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Without stress it's easy to look after a big section of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No pressure' strips P from KEEP to leave KEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The structural spine running along the bottom of a vessel is one of its parts.

clue.text: Decrepit sheep has to hobble

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to hobble or shackle an animal is to tie its legs

explanation.surface: An aged sheep has to have its legs tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbledown and falling apart, as a run-down building would be.

clue.text: Perish in passage, a nasty way to die

indicators.note: in puts the decaying word inside the gateway

parts.note: a gate is a passage through a wall or fence
to rot is to perish or decay

explanation.surface: Dying in a corridor sounds a grim end.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution by strangling with a cord or iron collar is an unpleasant method of death.

clue.text: Elite eatery brought up posh wines in container

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means the whole is read from bottom to top
in places the posh letter and the wines inside the container

parts.note: a bag is a container
U is the crossword letter for upper-class
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Fancy wines arriving at a smart restaurant in a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub with upmarket food is a superior place to eat.

clue.text: Play part on cross in cathedral? That's right

indicators.note: in puts the cross and the acting inside the cathedral city

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means coming after

parts.note: X is shaped like a cross
to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: An actor taking a role on the cross in a cathedral passion play.
explanation.definitionFit: Precisely so is an emphatic way of agreeing that someone is correct.

clue.text: Fish first to sink to the bottom after time delay

indicators.note: after means the fish follows the letter for time

indicators.text: first to sink to the bottom
indicators.note: the opening letter of the fish moves to its end, the bottom of a down answer

parts.note: sardines are small fish

explanation.surface: Fish lingers a while before the first ones drop to the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to sink to the bottom' moves S from the front of SARDINES to the end: ARDINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness is the quality of being delayed or slow.

clue.text: Good man churlishly giving up last dessert

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword abbreviation for a good man

indicators.note: giving up last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: churlishly means rudely

explanation.surface: A decent fellow grudgingly surrenders the final pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry roll filled with apple, from Austria, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Unorthodox young lady's announcement's in character, almost

indicators.note: in puts the advertisement inside the shortened character
almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character
an ad is a public announcement

explanation.surface: A rebellious girl's statement is nearly in keeping with her nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous young woman behaving like the lads breaks the conventional mould.

clue.text: Too frank, essentially: he didn't get a place

parts.note: also means too

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart of the word frank, its middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone was far too outspoken, at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is racing: finishing in the first few places; someone who ran but did not place is an also-ran.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse or competitor who ran but was unplaced; by extension any loser.

clue.text: Vigilante extremists blocking rum trade warded off

indicators.note: blocking means stuck in the middle, so the outer letters go inside
rum means strange, so the letters of trade are rearranged
extremists picks the outer letters of Vigilante

explanation.surface: Vigilantes stop smugglers running alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' means odd here, not the drink, rearranging the letters to ARTED around the vigilante's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned aside or prevented, as danger or a blow is turned away.

clue.text: Backward country's government relinquished control

indicators.note: relinquished means given up, so the letter is removed
backward means the country's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Niger is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An underdeveloped nation's administration gave up power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns NIGER into REGIN; 'relinquished' then takes out G.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap for steering a horse, and figuratively a means of restraint or authority.

clue.text: Four lines written about ordinary 1 down

definitions.note: the solution to 1 down names an off-white colour

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A quatrain written on everyday topics.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are pale yellowish-white shades, so the colour of tusks matches the colour of the milk's top.

clue.text: I lend an ear, desperate to get a booster

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the phrase's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A listener, frantic for a pick-me-up, promises to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released under stress gives the body a sudden boost of energy.

clue.text: Posh folk with no capital coming in

indicators.note: with no capital means losing its initial letter

parts.note: the gentry are upper-class people

explanation.surface: Penniless aristocrats arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of arriving or going in, a noun matching the gerund.

clue.text: Excursion to game taken up

indicators.note: in a down answer, taken up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: An outing to a match is arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip or journey round places is an outing.

clue.text: Post Office admitting stolen figure's a facsimile

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the stolen word goes inside

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
a stat is a statistic, a figure

explanation.surface: A post office lets in a stolen number, and it turns out to be a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark name for a photocopy, an exact reproduction of a document.

clue.text: On reduction of toll, tenor went on a bender

indicators.note: reduction of means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a knell is the toll of a bell
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: After a cut in the road charge, a singer celebrated with a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bender' looks like a drinking binge; it is one who bends, here the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on bended knee is a kind of bending, cheekily described as a bender.

clue.text: Jerseys may be kept here, we're told, for customer

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a byre is a cowshed, where Jersey cows would be kept

explanation.surface: A clothes shop's stockroom holds sweaters ready for the shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerseys are cows from the Channel Island, not sweaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchaser in a shop is a customer.

clue.text: The Parisian stopping goals needs cunning all the time

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the French article sits inside

parts.note: ends are aims or goals
le is French for the
sly means cunning

explanation.surface: A French goalkeeper saving shots needs constant craftiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Without ceasing means continually, at every moment.
